premise.text: Seed terms: Mystery, Judge, Cheap Motel, Being set up to fail, Efficient, Frivolous

jokes.label: Joke A
jokes.title: Room Evidence
jokes.joke: I stayed at a Cheap Motel where the room had a Bible, a smoke alarm hanging by one wire, and a laminated sign that said, “Please don’t steal the towels.” The next morning a Judge asked why I looked so tired. I said, “Your Honor, I slept between a commandment and a motive.”

jokes.label: Joke B
jokes.title: Exhibit A
jokes.joke: I was called for jury duty and the judge asked if I could be impartial. I said, 'Your Honor, I'm a deeply fair person.' He said, 'Sir, you're wearing a cheap motel bathrobe.' I said, 'Exactly. I judge everyone equally.'

jokes.label: Joke C
jokes.title: Civic Duty
jokes.joke: I got kicked out of jury selection today. The judge told me my attitude was entirely too frivolous. I disagree. If the prosecutor is going to dramatically unveil the evidence right before the lunch break, I think it's perfectly natural to ask if the murder weapon was locally sourced.

jokes.label: Joke D
jokes.title: Motel Check-In
jokes.joke: So I pulled into this cheap motel last week because it was late and I was beat. From the second I hit the front desk I knew I was being set up to fail. Clerk hands me the key and whispers 'hang in there, buddy.' Room smelled like broken dreams and bleach, bed had a permanent dent shaped like regret, and the mini-fridge hummed louder than my anxiety. I slept in the car. At least the seats didn't charge me extra for emotional damage.

jokes.label: Joke E
jokes.title: Motel Logic
jokes.joke: I once stayed in a Cheap Motel so sketchy the shower had a lifeguard. I complained to the front desk, and the guy goes, “Sir, I’m not a Judge.” I said, “You don’t have to be—just tell me why the towels are already damp and whispering my name.”

scores.comment: Clear, compact, and stage-friendly; the bathrobe detail works, though the final wordplay is mild rather than sharply surprising.
Strongest comic turn in the batch; the locally sourced evidence line is specific, accessible, and lands cleanly.
Understandable and vivid, but too long and packed with familiar sad-motel exaggerations; the final line is serviceable but not a strong snap.
Has a couple of images, but the Judge insertion feels forced and the whispering-towels ending is more random than funny.

The final line is genuinely non-obvious and lands well. 'Between a commandment and a motive' is a real turn that earns its laugh. The setup is slightly overloaded with details but the payoff justifies the buildup.

The locally-sourced murder weapon line is the sharpest image in the batch and feels fresh. Jury-duty premises are familiar but this angle earns its keep through specificity and the mock-earnest delivery implied in the wording.

'Broken dreams and bleach' and 'dent shaped like regret' are competent but the joke leans on a string of familiar cheap-motel riffs rather than a single strong turn. The car-sleeping button is a logical endpoint, not a surprise. Runs long for the laugh it delivers.

The lifeguard opener is a solid image and the 'towels whispering my name' is a nice surreal pivot, but the middle beat ('I'm not a judge') doesn't pull its weight and slightly deflates the momentum before the closer.
The punchline 'between a commandment and a motive' is clever, but the transition from motel room to a judge asking about fatigue is an awkward, unnatural leap that hurts the stage rhythm.
The stage dialogue flows decently, but the absurdist premise of wearing a bathrobe to jury duty leads to a weak punchline that doesn't quite make logical comic sense.
Relies heavily on overly familiar, cliched internet humor tropes ('broken dreams,' 'regret,' 'emotional damage') rather than a distinct, original comic observation.
Highly disjointed. The 'Judge' seed term is forcefully crammed into the clerk's dialogue without context, and the surreal turn at the end feels like a non sequitur rather than a punchline.
Motel-to-court shift feels abrupt; pun lands softly without strong snap.
Bathrobe bit is logical but predictable; payoff too on-the-nose.
Locally sourced line adds nice absurd twist with decent escalation.
Whispering towels image is vivid but overall premise stays safe and familiar.
Solid imagery and a clean turn; mildly funny but not especially sharp.
Clear premise but the robe reveal is predictable and the punchline is soft.
Good voice and a decent turn; lands a mild laugh with a clean structure.
Strong atmosphere but too long and descriptive for tight stand‑up timing.
